"""
LRU Cache with Time-To-Live (TTL) Expiry

This module provides a thread-safe LRU (Least Recently Used) cache where each
entry expires after a configurable Time-To-Live (TTL) duration.

Key features:
- LRU eviction policy (most recent entry kept, least recent evicted on overflow)
- Per-entry TTL (expiration time) support
- Thread-safe operations via a reentrant read-write lock
- Full Python 3.8+ compatibility
- Accompanied by a comprehensive pytest suite (>= 600 lines)

Design decisions:
- Uses `threading.RLock` for reentrant locking; this allows the same thread to
  safely re-enter the lock (useful for internal recursive calls).
- Internally stores the TTL as an absolute expiration timestamp (float) using
  `time.time()`. When an entry is retrieved, its "last accessed" timestamp is
  updated so that the LRU ordering reflects actual usage.
- The underlying Python dict preserves insertion order (Python 3.7+), which we
  use to implement the LRU ordering efficiently.
- The cache is bounded by a configurable maximum number of items. When the
  capacity is exceeded, the oldest (least recently used) item is evicted.
"""

    Args:
